decisions.reason: The bio-based bitumen binder remains a flagship of the firm's circular direction, and growth-generated slack lets management carry it while results are uncertain, though its distance from the plant-building core and the lack of evidence of market traction keep withdrawal risk elevated.

The infectious waste decontamination plant is close to the core WASTX line, backed by the ERMAFA partnership and positioned as a flagship, so management will keep evaluating it against aspirations rather than start problemistic search.
The mobile mechanical recycling plant is a low-cost modular extension of the established WASTX offer that fits the decentralized strategy, so there is little shortfall pressure to drop it.
